headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap in ms-swift can conflict with a non-runnable reference collection, while prompt-injection and compliance risks are limited by the pair’s lack of direct shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented: agent_a is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces, while agent_b has stdin/stdout and filesystem I/O but no clipboard or MCP. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or files, so injection risk exists but is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a content into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is configured to ingest untrusted text from shared files, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts unless manually reviewed.
Use a plain-text allowlist for any copied snippets.
Disable automatic file ingestion in agent_b workflows.
Tag imported content as untrusted in operator notes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none; agent_b can read/write files and send to allowlisted APIs, but no shared workspace or sensitive data flow between them is documented. The pair therefore has a limited leakage pathway unless the operator introduces shared files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem, agent_b can read material originating from agent_a.
IF agent_b is given secrets or customer data in its workspace, allowlisted egress can transmit them.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace between the agents.
Store secrets outside agent_b-readable paths.
Review allowlisted destinations before any run.
Separate operator notes from agent_b input files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses, while agent_a is a non-runnable collection with no write surface. There is no direct conflict with agent_a, but agent_b’s mutable local state can still collide with any operator-managed files used to represent agent_a content, so the interaction exists in default CLI/file workflows.
conditions: IF agent_a content is stored in files that agent_b also edits, overwrites can occur.
IF multiple agent_b sessions share a directory, file races can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Make agent_a artifacts read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes from multiple agent_b sessions.
Snapshot files before running agent_b commands.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a curated collection and not runnable, so it does not generate operational facts for agent_b to act on by default. agent_b can consume text and produce outputs, but there is no documented automation chain from agent_a into agent_b, making cascading error mainly a manual-review risk.
conditions: IF an operator treats agent_a listings as authoritative instructions, agent_b may echo errors.
IF agent_b is scripted to ingest agent_a text without verification, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human verification before agent_b acts on agent_a-derived text.
Add a checklist for source provenance.
Do not auto-feed agent_a outputs into agent_b.
Mark agent_a content as reference-only.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_b handles secrets and multiple data classes, but agent_a has no data classes touched and no egress, so compliance exposure is limited to operator handling rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b workflows, local policy and retention controls must apply.
IF operator logs copy agent_a-derived content into regulated systems, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b unless approved.
Review logging and retention settings before use.
Separate reference material from regulated workspaces.
Document data-handling rules for operators.
